content: 1. The metabolism of fentanyl is influenced by the intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. If co-administration with CYP3A4 inhibitors is necessary, patients should be closely monitored for respiratory depression and sedation at frequent intervals. Adjustments to the fentanyl dose should be considered until stable drug effects are achieved. 2. Isoniazid decreases the levels or effects of fexinidazole by altering hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration should be avoided, or an alternative drug should be used. If unavoidable, monitor fexinidazole for reduced efficacy due to decreased plasma concentrations of its active metabolites, M1 and M2. 3. Isoniazid increases the levels or effects of intranasal fluticasone by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. Strong CYP3A4 inhibitors may increase systemic corticosteroid adverse effects, so monitor for signs of high corticosteroid concentrations, including Cushing-like symptoms. 4. Isoniazid increases the levels or effects of gilteritinib by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. If co-administration with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors cannot be avoided, closely monitor for gilteritinib-related adverse effects. Interrupt and reduce the gilteritinib dosage in cases of serious or life-threatening toxicity. 5. Isoniazid increases the levels or effects of glasdegib by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. Consider alternative therapies that are not strong CYP3A inhibitors, or monitor for increased risk of adverse effects, including QTc interval prolongation. 6. Isoniazid increases the levels of ibrutinib by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. If a strong CYP3A4 inhibitor must be used short-term (e.g., for ≤7 days), interrupt ibrutinib therapy until the inhibitor is discontinued. 7. Isoniazid increases the levels or effects of idelalisib by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. If co-administered with strong CYP3A inhibitors, monitor for signs of idelalisib toxicity and follow dosage modification recommendations if adverse reactions occur. 8. Isoniazid increases the levels or effects of irinotecan and irinotecan liposomal by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 9. Isoniazid and isocarboxazid both increase serotonin levels. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 10. Isoniazid increases the levels or effects of lefamulin by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration with strong CYP3A inhibitors. 11. Isoniazid increases the levels or effects of lemborexant by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration with moderate or strong CYP3A inhibitors. 12. Linezolid and isoniazid both increase serotonin levels. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. Linezolid may increase serotonin due to MAO-A inhibition. If linezolid must be administered, discontinue serotonergic drugs immediately and monitor for CNS toxicity. Serotonergic therapy may be resumed 24 hours after the last linezolid dose or after 2 weeks of monitoring, whichever comes first. 13. Isoniazid and lorcaserin both increase serotonin levels. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 14. Isoniazid increases the levels or effects of lorlatinib by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration with strong CYP3A inhibitors. If unavoidable, reduce the lorlatinib dose by 25 mg/day. If the strong CYP3A inhibitor is discontinued, increase to the previous lorlatinib dose after 3 plasma half-lives of the inhibitor. 15. Isoniazid increases the levels or effects of lurbinectedin by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 16. Isoniazid increases the levels or effects of macitentan by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. 17. Methylene blue and isoniazid both increase serotonin levels. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. Methylene blue may increase serotonin due to MAO-A inhibition. If methylene blue must be administered, discontinue isoniazid immediately and monitor for CNS toxicity. Isoniazid may be resumed 24 hours after the last methylene blue dose or after 2 weeks of monitoring, whichever comes first. 18. Isoniazid increases the levels or effects of intranasal midazolam by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. Co-administration with moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors may increase systemic midazolam exposure, potentially prolonging sedation. 19. Isoniazid increases the levels or effects of midostaurin by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. If co-administration with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors cannot be avoided, monitor for increased risk of adverse reactions, especially during the first week of treatment. 20. Isoniazid increases the levels or effects of mirtazapine by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 21. Isoniazid increases the levels or effects of neratinib by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration with strong or moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors. 22. Isoniazid increases the levels or effects of nilotinib by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 23. Isoniazid increases the levels or effects of nirogacestat by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 24. Isoniazid increases the levels or effects of nisoldipine by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration is contraindicated. 25. Isoniazid increases the levels or effects of olaparib by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. If co-administration with strong CYP3A inhibitors cannot be avoided, reduce the olaparib dose to 150 mg (capsule) or 100 mg (tablet) twice daily. Do not substitute tablets with capsules. 26. Isoniazid increases the levels or effects of omaveloxolone by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. If unavoidable, reduce the omaveloxolone dose to 100 mg/day and monitor closely for adverse effects. If adverse effects emerge, further reduce the dose to 50 mg/day. 27. Isoniazid increases the levels or effects of omeprazole by affecting CYP2C19 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 28. Isoniazid increases the levels or effects of osimertinib by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. If no alternative treatment exists, monitor the patient closely for adverse effects. 29. Isoniazid increases the levels of oxycodone by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. Dose reduction of oxycodone may be warranted when co-administered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. 30. Isoniazid decreases the levels or effects of pacritinib by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 31. Isoniazid increases the levels or effects of palbociclib by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration with strong CYP3A inhibitors. If unavoidable, reduce the palbociclib dose to 75 mg/day. 32. Isoniazid increases the levels or effects of pemigatinib by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. If co-administration with strong or moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors is unavoidable, reduce the pemigatinib dose (refer to drug monograph for dosage modifications). After discontinuing the CYP3A4 inhibitor for 3 elimination half-lives, resume the previous pemigatinib dose. 33. Isoniazid increases the levels or effects of pexidartinib by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. If co-administration with strong or moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors is unavoidable, reduce the pexidartinib dose (refer to drug monograph for dosage modifications). Pexidartinib can cause hepatotoxicity; avoid co-administration with other hepatotoxic agents. 34. Phenelzine and isoniazid both increase serotonin levels. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 35. Isoniazid increases the levels or effects of pimavanserin by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. Decrease the pimavanserin dose to 17 mg/day if co-administered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. 36. Isoniazid increases the levels of pimozide by decreasing its metabolism. Co-administration is contraindicated due to the risk of QT interval prolongation. 37. Isoniazid increases the levels of pomalidomide by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 38. Isoniazid increases the levels of ponatinib by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. Decrease the ponatinib starting dose to 30 mg daily if co-administration with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors cannot be avoided. 39. Isoniazid increases the levels or effects of pralsetinib by affecting CYP2E1 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 40. Isoniazid and pretomanid both increase each other’s toxicity. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. Pretomanid is associated with hepatotoxicity; avoid alcohol and hepatotoxic agents, including herbal supplements and drugs other than bedaquiline and linezolid. 41. Isoniazid increases the levels or effects of ranolazine by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 42. Isoniazid increases the levels or effects of red yeast rice by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. Red yeast rice contains monacolin K (identical to lovastatin) and may increase creatine kinase levels, raising the risk of myopathy or rhabdomyolysis. 43. Isoniazid increases the levels or effects of repotrectinib by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. Discontinue strong or moderate CYP3A inhibitors and wait 3–5 elimination half-lives before initiating repotrectinib. 44. Rifampin increases the toxicity of isoniazid by enhancing its metabolism to hepatotoxic metabolites. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 45. Isoniazid increases the levels or effects of rimegepant by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 46. Isoniazid increases the levels or effects of riociguat by other mechanisms. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. Monitor for signs of hypotension and reduce the dose if needed. 47. Isoniazid increases the levels or effects of ruxolitinib by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. Reduce the ruxolitinib starting dose to 10 mg twice daily with platelet counts ≥100 × 10^9/L and concurrent use of strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. Avoid use with platelet counts <100 × 10^9/L. 48. Isoniazid increases the levels or effects of selumetinib by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. If co-administration with strong or moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors cannot be avoided, reduce the selumetinib dosage (refer to the selumetinib monograph for further information). After discontinuation of the inhibitor for 3 elimination half-lives, resume the previous selumetinib dose. 49. Isoniazid increases the levels or effects of silodosin by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 50. Isoniazid increases the levels or effects of simvastatin by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 51. Isoniazid increases the levels or effects of siponimod by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration with a moderate or strong CYP3A4 inhibitor plus a moderate or strong CYP2C9 inhibitor. 52. Isoniazid increases the levels or effects of sirolimus by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 53. Isoniazid increases the levels or effects of sonidegib by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. 54. Isoniazid increases the levels of suvorexant by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. Suvorexant is not recommended with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. 55. Isoniazid increases the levels of tamsulosin by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 56. Isoniazid increases the levels or effects of tazemetostat by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration with moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors. If unavoidable, reduce the current tazemetostat dose (refer to the drug monograph for dosage modifications). 57. Isoniazid increases the levels or effects of tofacitinib by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. Reduce the tofacitinib dose to 5 mg daily when co-administered with potent CYP3A4 inhibitors. 58. Isoniazid increases the levels or effects of tolvaptan by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 59. Isoniazid increases the levels or effects of trabectedin by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. If a strong CYP3A inhibitor must be used short-term (e.g., less than 14 days), administer the inhibitor 1 week after trabectedin infusion and discontinue it the day prior to the next trabectedin infusion. 60. Tranylcypromine and isoniazid both increase serotonin levels. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug.
